model.collision_kernel: hard spheres, b(z,omega)=|z dot omega|, Grad cutoff
model.scaling: epsilon partial_t f + v dot grad_x f = epsilon^(-2) Q(f,f)

claims.claim: There are smooth positive initial data on T^3 with unit local mass, zero local momentum, and local energy 3, such that epsilon^-2 H(f_epsilon^in|M)->0 but the order-three energy flux of g_epsilon^in diverges in distributions in x.
claims.quantifiers: For all sufficiently small epsilon>0, use a(x)=1+0.5 sin(2*pi*x_1), R=epsilon^-4, delta=epsilon^12 a(x), U=-delta R e_1/(1-delta), T=1-delta R^2/[3(1-delta)^2], and f=(1-delta)N(U,T I)+delta N(R e_1,I). Then epsilon^-2 H=O(epsilon^2), while pairing int (|v|^2/2)v M g_epsilon^in dv against grad cos(2*pi*x_1) equals -pi/(4 epsilon)+O(epsilon^11).
claims.dependency: Gaussian mass/momentum/energy identities; convexity of relative entropy; Gaussian KL and third-moment formulas.
claims.falsifier: An algebraic error in the exact Gaussian identities, entropy upper bound, or displayed flux pairing.
claims.scope: Falsifies entropy-only control of this flux passage. It does not prove that the hydrodynamic limit fails.

claims.claim: The same initial family converges entropically at order epsilon to g^in=0 in the local weak topology used by the cited theorem.
claims.quantifiers: Uniformly in x, ||f_epsilon^in(x,.)-M||_L1(dv)=O(epsilon^4); on every compact velocity set, g_epsilon^in->0 strongly in L1(dx dv); epsilon^-2 H(f_epsilon^in|M)->0=(1/2)int M|0|^2.
claims.dependency: Total-variation continuity of Gaussian densities for T near 1 and U near 0; tail mixture mass delta=O(epsilon^12).
claims.falsifier: Failure of local L1 convergence or of the stated entropy scaling for the given formula.
claims.scope: Initial-data entropic convergence only; no solution-level compactness is asserted.

claims.claim: The initial entropy convergence assumptions do not imply the initial-time analogue of the cited general-data Euler theorem's pointwise L2(M^-1) tail bound.
claims.quantifiers: For the data in C1 and every x, int M((f_epsilon^in-M)/M)^2 dv >= delta(x)^2 exp(R^2)-1 >= (epsilon^24/4)exp(epsilon^-8)-1 -> infinity.
claims.dependency: Gaussian chi-square identity for N(R e_1,I) relative to N(0,I), and f_epsilon^in>=delta N(R e_1,I).
claims.falsifier: A correction to the Gaussian likelihood-ratio integral or mixture lower bound.
claims.scope: Theorem 2.1 imposes its bound on the solution for almost every positive time. The t=0 calculation alone does not show that the actual solution violates that a.e.-in-time assumption; positive-time regularization is not analyzed here.

claims.claim: Saint-Raymond's 2009 Theorem 2.1 is a primary-source incompressible Euler limit for general entropically convergent initial fluctuations, with an additional uniform large-velocity bound on the solution family.
claims.quantifiers: For smooth bounded Omega or T^3 and a measurable a.e.-positive Grad-cutoff kernel 0<b(z,omega)<=Cb(1+|z|)^beta with int_S2 b(z,omega)domega>=Cb^-1|z|/(1+|z|), beta in [0,1], let q>1. Assume epsilon^-2 H(f_epsilon^in|M)<=C, g_epsilon^in weakly convergent locally and epsilon^-2 H->(1/2)int M|g^in|^2, plus int M((f_epsilon-M)/M)^2 dv<=C for a.e. (t,x). Then fluctuations are relatively weakly compact; each limit is an infinitesimal Maxwellian whose fields solve incompressible Euler and a transported thermal scalar, with a fast acoustic corrector and strong corrected L1_loc convergence, up to the target solution lifespan. The field data are rho^in=int M g^in, u^in=int v M g^in, theta^in=(1/3)int(|v|^2-3)M g^in; u(0)=P u^in and theta(0)=(3theta^in-2rho^in)/5.
claims.dependency: Saint-Raymond 2009, Theorem 2.1 and proof equations (3.29)-(3.35); collision entropy inequality; modulated entropy; tail/dissipation estimates; Lipschitz target flow.
claims.falsifier: A contrary theorem statement in the cited primary paper or a mismatch between its assumptions and this transcription.
claims.scope: Imported theorem statement; not independently re-proved. We instantiate q=2 and the hard-sphere kernel.

claims.claim: The high-velocity condition in the general-data theorem is used to close an energy-flux estimate that relative entropy alone cannot close.
claims.quantifiers: Saint-Raymond states that g_epsilon |v|^3 is not controlled by relative entropy and uses a Chapman-Enskog decomposition plus tail and entropy-dissipation control; for q>1 the proof gains epsilon^((q-1)/2), equal to epsilon^1/2 at q=2.
claims.dependency: Saint-Raymond 2009, discussion preceding Theorem 2.1 and proof equations (3.32)-(3.34); C1-C3 show entropy convergence does not itself control the flux.
claims.falsifier: A proof of the same distributional energy-flux bound from assumptions (a)-(b) alone, covering the explicit family in C1.
claims.scope: Indispensability is established for this flux-closure inference, not for the truth of Euler convergence under weaker hypotheses.

claims.claim: The 2003 well-prepared incompressible Euler theorem is consistent with the counterexample and does not identify the high-order flux at t=0.
claims.quantifiers: For smooth divergence-free u^in and epsilon^-2 H(f_epsilon^in|M_{1,epsilon u^in,1})->0, renormalized solutions with q>1 have fluctuation limits u dot v on the lifespan of the Lipschitz Euler solution. The constructed data meet this initial entropy condition for u^in=0.
claims.dependency: Saint-Raymond 2003, quoted as Theorem 1.2 in Saint-Raymond 2009; official Springer metadata and abstract.
claims.falsifier: A correction to the 2003 theorem assumptions or to H(f_epsilon^in|M)=O(epsilon^4).
claims.scope: Weak fluctuation convergence is compatible with a large instantaneous third moment; no theorem-level failure is claimed.

sources.citation: L. Saint-Raymond, Hydrodynamic limits: some improvements of the relative entropy method, Ann. Inst. H. Poincare Anal. Non Lineaire 26(3) (2009), 705-744.
sources.source_role: Primary theorem, assumptions, energy-flux discussion, entropy/dissipation proof chain.

sources.citation: L. Saint-Raymond, Convergence of Solutions to the Boltzmann Equation in the Incompressible Euler Limit, Arch. Rational Mech. Anal. 166 (2003), 47-80.
sources.source_role: Comparison theorem for well-prepared initial data.

open: No actual epsilon-dependent hard-sphere solution is constructed and analyzed through the initial layer.
No theorem-level failure of Euler convergence without the pointwise tail hypothesis is established.
Whether a weaker third-moment uniform-integrability condition plus the entropy-dissipation estimate suffices is unresolved here.
External correctness review and novelty/priority are UNKNOWN.
